title: Simulation of Refraction Through Voxel Volumes
summary: Ray tracing in X-ray science has typically been limited to descriptions where refraction occurs only at interfaces, ignoring the refraction occurring due to the continuous variations in index of refraction in the bulk of a material, as are common in biological samples like bone. We propose a method to simulate X-ray images directly on voxel grids using curved rays. We first validate this method compared to a model with an analytical solution, and then investigate the effects of voxel size, interpolation choice, and illumination to grid alignment on a few simulated test objects. From these investigations, we make several recommendations to guide simulations using these techniques.

title: DDA-Net: Accurate TDD Channel Estimation via Deep Unfolding the Doppler-Delay-Angle Representation of Channel Signals
summary: In TDD massive MIMO systems, channel estimation under sparse frequency-hopping pilots is challenging: each snapshot captures only one narrow pilot block that hops across frequency, with tens of milliseconds between adjacent snapshots. Finite-window leakage and off-grid effects weaken the ideal Doppler-delay-angle (DDA) sparsity, limiting both classical sparse recovery and purely data-driven approaches lacking an explicit structured transform-domain model. We propose DDA-Net, a model-driven 3D deep unfolding network for joint multi-snapshot channel state reconstruction. DDA-Net integrates an ADMM-based formulation with a closed-form data-consistency update that avoids tensor inversion, a lightweight Doppler-domain learned prior, and delay oversampling to mitigate basis mismatch. It consistently outperforms strong baselines across three channel settings from 3GPP TR 38.901: UMa-NLOS, UMi-NLOS, and CDL-B. Ablations confirm that window-level 3D processing and explicit Doppler modeling yield target-dependent improvements. With minimal target-domain fine-tuning, the UMa-pretrained model surpasses both its zero-shot version and counterparts trained from scratch with the same number of target-domain samples. The Doppler-domain design proves consistently superior to its time-domain equivalent, with a wider margin after fine-tuning. These results demonstrate that combining exact physical data consistency with a learned DDA-domain prior is an effective and sample-efficient approach to channel state acquisition under sparse frequency-hopping pilots.

title: Optimal symmetric low-rank BD-RIS configuration maximizing the determinant of a MIMO link
summary: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) significantly improve wireless performance by allowing tunable interconnections among elements, but their design in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems has so far relied on complex iterative algorithms or suboptimal approximations. This work introduces a simple yet powerful approach: instead of directly maximizing the achievable rate, we maximize the absolute value of the determinant of the equivalent MIMO channel. We derive a closed-form symmetric unitary scattering matrix whose rank is exactly twice the channel's degrees of freedom ($2r$). Remarkably, this low-rank solution achieves the same determinant value as the optimal unitary BD-RIS. Using log-majorization theory, we prove that the rate loss relative to the optimal unitary BD-RIS vanishes at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) or when the number of BD-RIS elements becomes large. Moreover, the proposed solution can be perfectly implemented using a $q$-stem BD-RIS architecture with only $q=2r-1$ stems, requiring a minimum number of reconfigurable circuits. The resulting Max-Det solution is orders of magnitude faster to compute than existing iterative methods while achieving near-optimal rates in practical scenarios. This makes high-performance BD-RIS deployment feasible even with large surfaces and limited computational resources.

title: DM-ASR: Diarization-aware Multi-speaker ASR with Unified Offline and Online Decoding with Large Language Models
summary: Multi-speaker automatic speech recognition (ASR) aims to recognize not only what was said, but also who said it and when. Recent Speech-LLMs have shown promising results in structured multi-speaker transcription, but jointly modeling speaker attribution, temporal information, and lexical content remains challenging and often requires substantial model capacity and training data. To address this challenge, we propose DM-ASR, a Diarization-aware Multi-speaker ASR framework that reformulates multi-speaker recognition as diarization-conditioned multi-turn dialogue generation. By leveraging diarization-derived speaker-time cues as explicit structural priors, DM-ASR decomposes transcription into a sequence of conditioned queries while preserving mixed acoustic information and conversational context. We further introduce optional word-level timestamps, fine-tune the model with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO), and analyze the complementary roles of diarization cues and language-model predictions. The proposed formulation also enables unified offline and causal sentence-level online decoding through flexible acoustic context and dialogue history management. Experiments on Mandarin and English benchmarks demonstrate competitive structured transcription performance with relatively compact models and training data, while effectively supporting both offline and online recognition.

title: Constrained Tensor Decomposition-Based Target Sensing for Sparse Non-Uniform Array-Enabled AFDM ISAC Systems
summary: Sparse non-uniform array-enabled affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising candidate for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), while its performance critically depends on accurate target parameter estimation. In this paper, we propose a constrained tensor decomposition-based sensing framework for delay, Doppler, and angle estimation. Specifically, a manifold-constrained alternating least squares algorithm is developed by exploiting the sparse array geometry structure, enabling robust factor matrix extraction and direct angle estimation. In addition, we analyze the uniqueness condition of the tensor decomposition. From the decomposed factor matrices, delays and Doppler shifts are coarsely estimated by pulse compression, and refined by an iterative one dimensional golden-section search.Moreover, the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) is derived to characterize the fundamental performance limit of the considered estimation problem. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed estimation algorithm.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing Over Deployed Telecommunication Fiber Networks: Challenges, Opportunities and Recent Advances
summary: This paper discusses key challenges and opportunities associated with deploying distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) over existing optical telecommunication networks. We review recent approaches to DAS interrogation and their compatibility with data transmission over deployed fibers, and present complementary investigations addressing three challenges: the influence of fiber-to-environment mechanical coupling, the single-shot extraction of distributed birefringence information using polarization-diversity DAS, and the impact of laser phase noise on continuous-wave phase-encoded DAS. These investigations rely on different forms of evidence: field measurements on a deployed telecommunication cable, laboratory experiments using fiber spools, and numerical simulations, respectively. The results illustrate complementary aspects of DAS deployment, from the interpretation of measured strain to polarization-sensitive sensing and phase-noise mitigation. They also highlight the need for further validation and integration of these approaches under operational telecommunication-network conditions.

title: Deep Pseudo-Proximal Map: A Self-Supervised Data-Fitting Agent for Iterative Reconstruction
comments: To appear in 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers
summary: Iterative algorithms for inverse imaging problems split reconstruction into alternating subproblems, one of which requires evaluating the data-fitting proximal map. In many practical cases, this proximal map has no analytic solution and so must be approximated by an inner loop solver at every iteration, compounding the cost of the outer reconstruction loop. To address this, we propose the pseudo-proximal map (PPM), a reformulation of the data-fitting proximal map as the minimum mean square error estimate of a synthetic probabilistic model. We implement the deep PPM as a self-supervised neural network trained only on sampled Gaussian noise, requiring no ground-truth training images. The deep PPM can be trained for any operator for which the forward model $A$ and its transpose $A^T$ can be evaluated, with provable equivalence to the proximal map when $A$ is linear. We validate the deep PPM on Gaussian deblurring and 4x super-resolution, where the proximal map has an analytic solution, and on X-ray computed tomography (XCT), where no analytic solution exists. Used as the data-fitting agent within an iterative reconstruction method, the deep PPM reproduces the reference reconstruction to within 1% NRMSE for all three operators, and for XCT, it replaces the inner conjugate-gradient loop with a single network evaluation that is 18x faster.
comment: To appear in 2026 Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems, and Computers

title: Sensing-Assisted OFDM with Index Modulation: A Waveform for Optical Wireless Integrated Communication and Localisation
summary: This paper proposes sensing-assisted OFDM with index modulation (SA-OFDM-IM) for joint communication and localisation over optical wireless systems. In SA-OFDM-IM, a multilayer frequency-domain architecture partitions each layer's admissible subcarriers into disjoint communication and distributed sensing-pilot subsets, applying group-wise index modulation (IM) within the communication subset. A constrained sensing-to-communication energy allocation jointly minimises average bit-error rate (BER) and delay-based localisation root mean square error (RMSE) under a minimum power-domain margin, enabling low-complexity, ordered-energy detection of both sensing and communication subcarriers without exhaustive maximum-likelihood search. Sensing tones are aggregated across the frame to reconstruct the channel frequency response, yielding the line-of-sight (LoS) delay tap and phase-compensated LoS gain for multilateration and, via the proposed delay-aided received signal strength (RSS) refinement. Simulation results indicate that SA-OFDM-IM can achieve up to 5 dB lower SNR requirement in BER and up to three orders of magnitude lower channel-estimation error than DC-biased optical OFDM, while the RSS estimator removes the SNR-independent error floors of delay-only and hybrid-RSS benchmarks to attain sub-delay-bin range and position accuracy, remaining robust under random known and unknown receiver orientations.

title: Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort
comments: Original article. Submitted to Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (JMRI)
summary: Radiomic features derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are sensitive to scanners; therefore, they require harmonization across scanners. In a radiomic feature dataset, some batches may be severely underrepresented compared to the others e.g., the Erasmus Glioma Database, which may provide harmonized features biased towards the larger batches in the dataset. We investigated whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before empirical-Bayes ComBat estimation improves feature harmonization and reduces residual scanner association while retaining grade-related information. In this retrospective, the Erasmus Glioma Database included 733 eligible patients acquired at a single center across nine vendor-by-field-strength configurations. Structural MRI acquired at 1 T, 1.5 T, and 3 T; four structural MRI sequences were analyzed. From four structural MRI sequences, 428 features were computed using an IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics implementation. The sample sizes of some scanner batches were very small compared to others, which may produce unequal precision and shrinkage of batch-effect estimates. We proposed a data augmentation approach to overcome the limitation of ComBat. We provided exploratory evidence, along with confirmatory Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction to assess the proposed method. Before harmonization, 392/428 features (91.6%) differed significantly across scanner batches (median eta-squared=0.463). Standard ComBat reduced this to 13/428 (3.0%), whereas batch-augmented ComBat reduced it to 8/428 (1.9%); the median residual effect size was <0.001 for both harmonized conditions. Batch augmentation appeared to be a useful strategy to improve the performance of ComBat for feature harmonization under severe batch-size imbalance.
comment: Original article. Submitted to Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (JMRI)

title: When Do Sports Leagues Stop Being Competitive? Bayesian Detection of Competitive-Balance Eras from Match-Level Data
summary: Competitive balance shapes outcome uncertainty, fan interest, and league regulation, yet standard measures summarize realized standings and cannot separate structural ability differences from match-level randomness. We develop a Bayesian framework that infers structural competitive balance from longitudinal match outcomes. Team abilities are obtained by projecting Gaussian auxiliary variables onto a graph-fused l1 polytope whose radius measures total pairwise ability variation. The projection places positive probability on exact ties, so statistically indistinguishable teams form explicit rank tiers. The radius equals realized ability variation whenever the constraint binds, linking it to parity, detectability, and structural inequality. An adaptive finite-regime model lets competitive eras recur, emerge, and disappear while team hierarchies remain season specific. Simulations show accurate recovery of regimes, radii, abilities, and tiers. Applied to 25 English Premier League seasons, the model identifies a persistent shift to a more stratified league beginning in 2005/06, with 2010/11 the only later return to the compressed regime. It also shows that a close title race can coexist with wide league-wide separation and that head-to-head results can separate clubs level on points. The framework gives leagues a model-based measure of balance to inform debates on revenue sharing and financial regulation.

title: Bayesian Spatio-temporal Modeling of Multi-Site Wastewater Surveillance Data
summary: Wastewater surveillance provides population-level evidence of infectious disease activity. As surveillance expands across multiple sites, repeated measurements must be analyzed jointly while accounting for differences among sites and the public health regions they represent. We develop a Bayesian spatio-temporal framework that decomposes wastewater measurements into a shared epidemic curve, spatially correlated regional deviations, persistent site effects, and within-site temporal dependence. This hierarchical decomposition accommodates unequal observation windows and sampling schedules, allowing regional trajectories to be compared while preserving site-level heterogeneity. A direct marginal spatial covariance specification further separates the magnitude of regional variation from the strength of association between neighboring regions, providing distinct interpretations of these two sources of spatial variation. We also introduce region-specific time shifts to distinguish regional leads and lags in epidemic timing from differences in signal levels and local fluctuations. Simulation studies demonstrate the recovery of these components and show that omitting true time shifts can lead to increased estimates of residual temporal variation. Application to Ontario SARS-CoV-2 wastewater surveillance data reveals persistent site heterogeneity, within-site temporal dependence, and spatial association among neighboring regions. Regional timing differences are more pronounced during the first year of Omicron than in the XBB-and-later period.

title: Stay, Reposition, or Recharge: Battery-Aware Operation of Robotaxi Fleets
summary: Electric robotaxis are rapidly expanding from pilots to scaled commercial deployment; unlike traditional human-driven ride-hailing vehicles, they require centralized fleet control and careful management of vehicle state of charge (SoC). We study how a fleet manager should jointly make service, empty repositioning, idling, and charging decisions in such systems. We develop a continuous-time fluid model in which vehicles evolve across location-charge states, and identify two forms of charge-aware control that are absent from classic repositioning models: early return-to-depot (RTD) and charge-aware repositioning. In particular, the optimal solution admits simple threshold structures. Each location has a battery threshold such that vehicles should return to the depot to recharge when their SoC is below it and should not do so when their SoC is above it. Vehicles should not reposition below the same threshold either; above it, the choice of destination depends on whether a vehicle's SoC matches the destination's battery sensitivity, a notion we introduce in the paper. We then quantify the value of charge awareness by comparing fully charge-aware policies with charge-oblivious policies that ignore SoC in RTD and repositioning decisions. We show that the performance gap can be unbounded, driven by a dilemma between under-utilizing high-charge vehicles and over-sending low-charge vehicles to locations from which charging is costly. A numerical case study calibrated using 2025 NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission trip records illustrates these thresholds and shows that charge-aware control can generate substantial gains in a realistic urban network. Importantly, simple threshold-based heuristics recover most of the value of the fully charge-aware solution.

title: Unobserved Consideration and Consumer Welfare
summary: Can welfare effects of price change be identified when consumers' consideration sets are heterogeneous and unobserved? We establish that the welfare distribution is the same functional of structural choice probabilities under stable but limited consideration as under full consideration. The result permits unrestricted income-effects, preference heterogeneity, and dependence between preferences and consideration. Within this class, limited consideration admits a full-consideration representation preserving choice-probabilities and money-metric compensation: consideration/preferences can remain unidentified while demand and welfare are identified. When consideration sets contract as prices rise, the welfare distribution can be bounded using demand and a bound on choice-set attrition.

title: MSR-CP: A Modified Segmented Regression Approach to Change Point Estimation in Rainfall Patterns in West Bengal
summary: This study presents a methodology for detecting change point in precipitation series using a smooth version of segmented regression model. We examine several existing change point detection methods and identify their limitations in capturing gradual changes commonly observed in climate data. To address these limitations, we discuss an extension of the traditional segmented regression model enabling the detection of gradual shifts in trend. The developed methodology is further extended to accommodate dependent error structures, which are common in time series data. Extensive simulation studies are conducted to evaluate the performance and computational efficiency of the proposed approach relative to existing methods. The methodology is subsequently applied to 60 years of monsoon rainfall data from two districts of West Bengal, India. This approach offers improved insights into evolving rainfall patterns and serves as a useful tool for climate data analysis and long-term forecasting.

title: Intensity-Based Estimation of Extreme Value Models for Highly Censored Data via a Latent Poisson Process
summary: Extreme value theory provides a natural framework for modelling rare events and extrapolating tail probabilities, but its direct application to survival analysis is complicated by right censoring, heterogeneous follow-up, and the need for coherent inference beyond the range of the observed data. We propose a Bayesian survival model that integrates extreme value theory with a hazard-based formulation built upon the extended generalized Pareto distribution. Rather than separating the bulk and tail of the distribution through an explicit threshold, the proposed model represents the entire hazard function within a unified parametric framework, allowing moderate and extreme survival times to be analysed simultaneously while preserving the asymptotic tail behaviour implied by extreme value theory. Inference is performed through a two-stage procedure. We further develop bias-correction procedures based on latent representative locations and adaptive partition refinement, and establish theoretical results showing the asymptotic consistency of the proposed approximation under standard regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the methodology provides reliable uncertainty quantification across a wide range of tail regimes, censoring proportions, and sample sizes, while remaining robust under moderate model misspecification. The practical performance of the approach is illustrated through an analysis of a heart failure cohort, where the proposed model enables inference on long-term survival probabilities and tail behaviour beyond the observed follow-up period. The resulting framework offers a computationally feasible and theoretically grounded alternative for modelling censored survival data when inference on extreme survival times is of primary scientific interest.

title: Bounded GARCH Processes
summary: We propose a novel class of Bounded GARCH (B-GARCH) processes designed to characterise the conditional heteroskedasticity of continuous time series constrained within a compact interval. While standard GARCH specifications are tailored for R-valued data, many empirical series, such as realised correlation, unemployment rates, expenditure shares, and relative humidity, are bounded. Fitting a traditional GARCH model to such data creates a severe support mismatch, frequently generating predictions and density forecasts that breach the natural boundaries of the data (boundary violation). Furthermore, conventional approaches utilising non-linear link transformations onto the real line might induce interpretability issues and estimation biases. To address these limitations, our proposed B-GARCH framework ensures a proper predictive distribution and an equation for the dynamic conditional variance with a parameter constraint that strictly preserves the bounded support of the entire process almost surely. We establish the fundamental probabilistic properties of the process, proving strict stationarity and ergodicity, and address parameter estimation via conditional maximum likelihood. The asymptotic consistency and normality of the estimators are rigorously derived, and their finite-sample performance is validated through Monte Carlo simulations. An empirical application to the monthly realised correlation between the Vanguard Real Estate ETF (VNQ) and the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) demonstrates that B-GARCH models effectively capture volatility clustering while completely eliminating boundary violation issue that plagues traditional GARCH models.

title: Fast Functional Clustering via Closed-Form Covariance Updates
summary: Functional clustering identifies coordinated molecular profiles, but repeated numerical covariance optimization can make mixture-model fitting computationally demanding. We develop a fast functional clustering procedure for joint analysis across conditions, combining linear mean profiles on a standardized log niche coordinate with first-order structured antedependence (SAD(1)) covariance. Weighted residual statistics yield closed-form conditional covariance updates under four parameter-sharing specifications, while an innovation representation simplifies likelihood evaluation. In same-R comparisons with numerical optimization of identical conditional objectives, the closed-form solver was 91.5--201.4 times as fast, with objective agreement in all 60 targets. Under matched complete mixture fits, it achieved a 1.87--2.37-fold speedup with identical cluster assignments. Recovery simulations showed higher module classification accuracy and lower mean-curve error than $K$-means and a Gaussian mixture with shared full covariance when the mean structure was correctly specified. SAD(1) provided an additional recovery gain under strong residual correlation, whereas curved-mean controls identified the importance of an appropriate mean family. Applications to single-condition gut microbiota, paired leaf--root microbiota and three-visit human gut multi-omics illustrate the framework across different numbers of conditions. Closed-form covariance estimation makes joint functional clustering substantially faster while retaining the fitted model's likelihood and assignments.

title: Improving Minority Population Sampling with BISG Probabilities: Evidence from a Survey of Jewish Americans
summary: Sampling geographically dispersed minority populations poses substantial challenges when individual group membership cannot be directly observed. Although stratified sampling can offer efficiency gains, these gains are typically modest unless the minority population is highly concentrated within a small number of strata. In this paper, we propose using Bayesian Improved Surname Geocoding (BISG) to enhance the efficiency of minority population sampling. BISG generates individual-level probabilities of minority group membership based on names and residential addresses. We incorporate these probabilities into a stratified Poisson probability sampling design. Applying the proposed approach to a national survey of Jewish Americans, we find that our estimates closely align with those from a large-scale Pew Research Center survey of the same population, which relied on a substantially more expensive sampling strategy involving geographic stratification and screening. At a fraction of the cost, our survey reproduces nearly identical patterns observed by Pew, including estimates of religious denomination prevalence and participation in specific religious activities.

title: A Poisson Factor Mixture Model for the Analysis of Linguistic Competence
summary: Dependence among variables and unobserved heterogeneity are common features of multivariate count data. We propose a model-based clustering approach for this setting based on a Poisson factor mixture model, which combines a low-dimensional latent structure with a finite mixture specification. This enables simultaneous dimension reduction and clustering while providing interpretable latent representations of count profiles. The proposal originates from the UniversITA project, which collected formal written texts from a representative sample of Italian university students. Since university students play a central role in the process of linguistic change, as they are the most educated segment of the youth population, understanding variation in their writing is substantively important for both language research and higher education policy. Texts were annotated for various linguistic features, producing multivariate count data. The fitted model identifies two correlated latent dimensions of writing competence, interpretable as communicative effectiveness and grammatical-linguistic control. Incorporating educational and sociodemographic covariates further reveals distinct student profiles associated with field of study and prior educational background. Beyond this application, the proposed framework can be employed for the analysis of heterogeneous multivariate count data with complex dependence patterns, such as those arising in educational assessments, psychological and behavioral studies, and text analysis.

title: The Earth Moves, But So Does the Bias: Systematic Upward Bias of the Wasserstein (Earth Mover's) Distance and Permutation-Based Null Calibration
comments: This version was submitted to Political Analysis (R&R) on October 12, 2026. The first submission was made on May 21, 2026. It was accepted on November 4, 2026
summary: The Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) is gaining increasing interest among political scientists for assessing similarity in preference distributions. Existing applications predominantly involve relatively large samples and low-dimensional response spaces, which can mitigate finite-sample distortions. However, empirical EMD remains biased upward due to sampling variation in empirical probability measures. This problem is often overlooked and becomes especially severe in high-dimensional or sparse settings, including conjoint distributions that serve as an illustrative example in this paper. As political scientists are broadening their use cases of EMD, this paper cautions against interpreting standard bootstrap uncertainty bounds as a correction for the upward bias of empirical EMD. It proposes a permutation-based null calibration framework for more robust hypothesis testing. As a non-parametric approach, it frees researchers from making directional or distributional shape assumptions. While alternative estimators require these rigid assumptions to correct for upward bias, political science data often fail to meet them in practice. Through four sets of Monte Carlo simulations, this paper demonstrates the utility of this framework. The proposed approach also applies more generally to empirical comparisons of two probability distributions defined on a common metric space, provided that the ground distance between support points is substantively meaningful.

title: GPU-accelerated Regularized Vector Multiplicative Error Models for Positive-valued Financial Time Series
comments: ISBIS-STATFIN Conference 2026 contributed talk (Conference link: https://statfin.cmi.ac.in/ISBIS2026/, Talk link: https://statfin.cmi.ac.in/ISBIS2026/#:~:text=72-,Rohan%20Chattre,-UConn)
summary: The logarithmic vector multiplicative error model (log-vMEM) provides a methodology for modeling and forecasting multivariate positive-valued time series. However, the number of autoregressive parameters increases rapidly with the system dimension and lag order, posing challenges for estimation and model selection. This paper develops a regularized estimation framework for the log-vMEM with multivariate Gamma errors by incorporating hierarchical lag structures to induce sparsity and accommodate heterogeneous lag dynamics. We consider three hierarchical lag structures: componentwise, own-other, and elementwise, in combination with group lasso, group MCP, and group SCAD, adaptive group lasso penalties. Parameter estimation is carried out through an alternating block-coordinate optimization algorithm with sequential Gauss-Seidel updates, while GPU-accelerated numerical quadrature is employed to address the computational burden of evaluating the multivariate Gamma likelihood. Simulation experiments investigate parameter recovery and lag selection under different sparsity structures. The real data analysis is carried out on the realized volatility measures for Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) which allows a comparison of the competing regularization approaches in an empirical financial setting. Together, these developments provide a computational framework for sparse multivariate volatility modeling with flexible lag structures and dependent Gamma errors.

title: When Statisticians Can Also Be AI Engineers, What Could We Build?
summary: Statistical software makes methods widely available. Good statistical work, however, requires understanding the question, how the data were collected, and what conclusions the evidence can support. As AI agents make data analysis accessible to people without statistical training, this reasoning should be built into the systems themselves. Our review of selected AI agents for data analysis and study design points to a gap in documented support for scientific inquiry with users at runtime. In this paper, we advocate designing domain-specific interactive harnesses in which statistical principles guide proactive inquiry: agents recognize missing information that could change an analysis, ask questions users may not know to raise, and use the answers to guide or revise analytical decisions. Two practical entry points illustrate how statisticians can begin building: an implemented causal-consulting skill within an existing agent environment and Model Forge, a custom harness for interactive model and algorithm development. These design examples connect statistical principles to choices about context, memory, tools, and interfaces, and motivate evaluation of both computational correctness and the scientific consequences of interaction. We conclude with a broader interdisciplinary research agenda on adaptive human-agent interaction, including selective information acquisition, evolving user preferences, and evaluation under uncertainty.

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
comments: Keywords: Stochastic exponential; true martingale; strict local martingale; multi-dimensional diffusion; Fichera drift; Feller's test; Khasminskii's criterion; stochastic volatility; affine and Wishart processes; uniqueness for degenerate parabolic equations
summary: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate bounded above and away from zero. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.

title: A Rough Instantaneous Squared VIX Model for Term Structure and Option Pricing
summary: The VIX term structure provides forward-looking measures of market uncertainty across horizons, while VIX options allow investors to hedge volatility risk. This paper proposes a rough instantaneous squared VIX (RISVIX) model by introducing fractional memory into the conventional Markovian framework. We derive an explicit representation of the VIX term structure governed by Mittag--Leffler decay and a semi-closed-form pricing formula for VIX options based on an affine Fourier--Laplace transform. These results support a two-step calibration procedure that estimates memory, mean reversion, and date-specific initial states from VIX term-structure indices before calibrating the remaining distributional parameters to VIX option prices. Using daily VIX term-structure indices and VIX option quotes from January 2018 to June 2025, we find that RISVIX improves upon the Markovian benchmark in fitting the VIX term structure, with larger gains during elevated-volatility periods and for its slope and curvature. RISVIX also improves out-of-sample option pricing, reducing MSE and MAE by 13.06\% and 6.33\%, respectively, with larger gains at shorter maturities and in high-VIX states. These findings suggest that the gains from fractional memory are particularly pronounced when volatility is elevated and can be obtained within a tractable direct model of VIX derivatives. Comparisons with additional benchmarks from the recent literature also show improvements to varying degrees in both VIX term-structure fitting and option pricing.

title: On consistency of optimal portfolio choice for state-dependent exponential utilities
summary: In a complete Brownian market, we characterize consistency across investment horizons for state-dependent exponential utilities. We show that consistency is equivalent to an explicit relation between the drift and diffusion of risk tolerance and a deterministic absolutely continuous function. Within this family, the forward performance property selects a unique coefficient. More generally, under the stated admissibility conditions, a forward performance is consistent, whereas consistency alone does not imply the forward performance property.

title: Why financial prices exhibit Brownian motion despite predictable order flow: An exactly solvable nonlinear price impact model
summary: In econophysics, there are two enigmatic empirical laws of financial market microstructure: (i) the market-order flow has predictable persistence due to metaorder splitting by institutional investors, as formulated by the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model. However, this phenomenon seems paradoxical given the diffusive and unpredictable price dynamics. (ii) The price impact $I(Q_{\rm tot})$ of a large metaorder $Q_{\rm tot}$ follows the square-root law, $I(Q_{\rm tot})\propto \sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}$. In this Letter, we reveal why price dynamics follows Brownian motion despite predictable order flow by unifying these enigmas via an exactly solvable model. We generalize the Lillo--Mike--Farmer model to nonlinear price-impact dynamics, which is mapped to a solvable Lévy-walk model. Our exact solution shows that the price dynamics remains diffusive under the square-root law, even under persistent order flow, reflecting the finite variance of metaorder impact; our model is thus a minimal representative of the universality class of nonlinear price-impact models with finite-variance metaorder impact. This work illustrates the crucial role of the square-root law in mitigating price movements by large metaorders, leading to Brownian price dynamics, consistent with the efficient market hypothesis over long timescales.

title: Reaction-boundary variance and adjoint-consistent local-volatility projection
comments: 16 pages, 12 figures, 1 table; minor clarifications, updated references, expanded discussion and limitations, results unchanged; Code reproducibility see:https://github.com/timgebbie/reaction-boundary-vol-surface-reproducibility
summary: We derive an operational-time variance kernel for a latent-order-book reaction boundary and use it to separate three objects usually collapsed in calendar-time volatility models: a structural boundary cumulant, a clock projection, and a pricing-measure choice. The reaction boundary is the zero of a bid--ask imbalance field. For a locally linear book, signed order-flow perturbations displace this zero through a damped Abel response kernel, so the variance of boundary increments is obtained as a finite-scale Green-function cumulant rather than introduced as a primitive diffusion coefficient. For long-memory forcing with exponent $0<γ<1$, the operational variance has a closed asymptotic form involving effective signed-forcing intensity, liquidity slope, resilience, memory, and operational coarse-graining scale. A deterministic activity clock gives the benchmark local-volatility projection. More general, non-unique clocks generate candidate calendar-time pricing systems. We argue that such projections are admissible only when the induced forward density operator and backward valuation operator remain adjoint on the same state space. Adjoint consistency is therefore a reality constraint on operational-to-calendar time projection: it disciplines non-unique time and identifies where incompleteness enters.
